page.answer: Short answer. The best solar generator for home use is the BLUETTI Apex 300 with a B300K battery. It gives 5,529.6 Wh and 3,840 W from one box, and BLUETTI rates it for 6,000 cycles to 80%. The Anker F3800 Plus gives 3,300 W on its own. Its 6,000 W needs an expansion battery.

What the differences mean

Dealectric does not test units. The figures below come from the makers' pages, from the named reviewers, or from the arithmetic shown.

  • Cost per Wh, today's maker prices: Apex 300 + B300K is $2,599 / 5,529.6 Wh = $0.47/Wh. Apex 300 alone is $1,499 / 2,764.8 Wh = $0.54/Wh. Explorer 5000 Plus is $3,499 / 5,040 Wh = $0.69/Wh. The F3800 Plus is sold only in a kit today: $4,799.99 / 3,840 Wh = $1.25/Wh.
  • Getting the F3800 Plus to 6,000 W: one box gives 3,300 W. Adding one BP3800 at $1,999.99 adds 6,000 − 3,300 = 2,700 W.
  • Rated lifetime energy, as an upper bound that ignores capacity fade: Apex 300: 6,000 × 2.7648 kWh = 16,589 kWh, ending at 80%. DELTA Pro 3: 4,000 × 4.096 kWh = 16,384 kWh, ending at 80%. Explorer 5000 Plus: 4,000 × 5.04 kWh = 20,160 kWh, ending at 70%. F3800 Plus: 3,000 × 3.84 kWh = 11,520 kWh, with no end capacity stated.
  • Measured energy out: OutdoorGearLab got 3,790 Wh out of the DELTA Pro 3: 3,790 / 4,096 = 92.5%. Outdoor Life got 2,290 Wh out of the Apex 300: 2,290 / 2,764.8 = 83%.
  • Idle cost per day: Apex 300: 20 W × 24 h = 0.48 kWh (The Solar Lab). Explorer 5000 Plus, inverter on: 58 W × 24 h = 1.39 kWh (The Solar Lab).
  • A 200 W fridge, router and lights: Apex 300 + B300K: 5,529.6 × 0.83 / 200 = 23 h. This assumes the bundle delivers at the 83% Outdoor Life measured on the Apex 300 alone. DELTA Pro 3: 3,790 / 200 = 19 h.

One box versus the headline number

Several of these stations advertise a power figure that one box delivers only under certain conditions. Anker's F3800 Plus page carries a footnote: "3,300W for single unit, 6,000W when working with 1 or more expansion batteries." The same page says the 240 V output cannot be used while the unit charges from 120 V AC. Jackery's 7,200 W comes only from the L14-30R/14-50 outlet. The four 120 V outlets top out at 3,600 W. The DELTA Pro 3 gives 4,000 W, but StormWatts reports that its 120 V and 240 V outputs work one at a time. BLUETTI says one Apex 300 gives 3,840 W and can power 120 V and 240 V devices at the same time.

The cycle ratings also end at different points. BLUETTI rates the Apex 300 for 6,000 cycles to 80% capacity. EcoFlow rates the DELTA Pro 3 for 4,000 cycles to 80%. Jackery's spec gives 4,000 cycles to 70% for the Explorer 5000 Plus. Anker states "3,000+ cycles" with no end capacity.

Measured results: OutdoorGearLab's Kenji Mowrey got 3,790 Wh out of the DELTA Pro 3 (review dated 2026-01-13). Outdoor Life's Laura Lancaster got 2,290 Wh out of the Apex 300 running a dehumidifier. The Solar Lab measured about 20 W idle on the Apex 300 and about 58 W on the Explorer 5000 Plus with the inverter on. The Solar Lab's Explorer 5000 Plus also struggled to start an air conditioner with a 10,000 W surge. We could not find a named test of delivered energy for the Explorer 5000 Plus or the F3800 Plus, or a named idle measurement with a stated method for the DELTA Pro 3 or the F3800 Plus. For those, use the rated figures and the arithmetic above.

Availability on 2026-11-15: BLUETTI's Apex 300 page says the unit is expected to ship in late January, though the BLUETTI store listed the Apex 300 + B300K bundle as available. Jackery lists the Explorer 5000 Plus as a pre-order shipping Nov 28. The DELTA Pro 3 did not appear in EcoFlow's US store search.

Not recommended

Don't buy a single Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus for its 6,000 W. On its own it gives 3,300 W, which is less than an Apex 300 or a DELTA Pro 3. It also drops its 240 V output while charging from a 120 V outlet. On 2026-11-15 Anker listed the station alone as sold out and offered it only in a $4,799.99 Smart Home Power Kit.
